- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; increase forecast slope gently to align with sentiment turn.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before projecting.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 5–10% gap), model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days unless sentiment strongly supports upside.
